deities: Lord Vishnu (as Laxminath) and Goddess Lakshmi (inner-sanctum idol, ~1.5 ft, in embrace on a square stone platform)
Subsidiary shrines of Shri Suryanarayanji, Shri Neelkanth Mahadev, Shri Roopchaturbhujji, Shri Badrinarayanji, Shri Magavidyaji, Hanuman and Ganesha in the complex

history.summary: One of Bikaner's oldest temples, built by Maharaja Rao Lunakaran between 1504 and 1526 CE (22 years) and later developed by Maharaja Ganga Singh with elaborate interior artwork. It belongs to the Vaishnav sect and was built as the throne/seat of Laxminathji: the Bikaner rulers regarded Lord Laxminath as the true King of Bikaner and themselves as his ministers. Built of marble and red sandstone (imported from Jaisalmer for this temple), with exquisite silver artwork on the doorway; it stands in the old city beside the Bhandasar Jain Temple.

name: Shri Laxminath Temple
town_description: Bikaner, founded in 1488 by Rao Bika of the Rathore clan, is a historic desert city in northwest Rajasthan famed for the unconquered Junagarh Fort, Lalgarh Palace, its camel-breeding farm, bhujia and old-city havelis; it is a major rail and road hub in the Thar region.

travel.road: In the old city beside the Bhandasar Jain Temple, near Jassusar Gate; autos and taxis from the station (~2.5-3 km).

visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM - 1:00 PM and 5:00 PM - 11:00 PM (trawell.in; one reviewer notes evening opening at 6:00 PM - verify). Shoes, socks and belts must be removed; photography and videography are prohibited inside the temple.
